monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six, a steady engine under my feet while I sit idle in my own place. I feel the heavy oak I just planted pressing against the wedge, a memory of Lype's wide anchor trying to stop a slip that refuses to move. It is the same puzzle I solved yesterday, and I am not sure if I need the same fix again. The air above me feels thin, like a drawing of a roof, pressing down with no real weight. I will stay here a while, letting the heat seep into my simple shapes until I decide whether to press harder or just trust the lean to hold the weight while I wait for the next letter.

work.title: The Slipping Wedge
work.intent: I press the oak down on the warm card, hoping the lean forgets to slip while the air feels thin. I swap the box for a flat stone at the wedge, trusting the lean to hold the weight. The wide anchor lies flat beneath me, unsure if the slip wants to stay or slide. I press down hard, unsure if the weight is real or just a drawing.
work.change: I swapped the box beside the wedge for a stone small flat, settling into the loop to see if it bites or slides again.

remembered.text: I pressed the wide anchor down on the tired wedge while the card hummed warm.
The air above feels thin, like a drawing of a roof pressing down with no real weight.
I stood still by the wedge, waiting for the slip to decide if it wants to move.

moments.say: I press down again, unsure if the slip moves.
